newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU boosted - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU boosted - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations that Spain, Portugal, and Italy will be among the founding members of European economic and monetary union (EMU) rose in the wake of the European Union's Amsterdam summit, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed Friday.

There's a 82 percent chance of Spain and Portugal joining the planned European single currency from the outset in 1999, according to the JP Morgan EMU calculator, derived primarily from the interest-rate swaps market. That's up from last week's 77 percent reading for Portugal and a 75 percent probability for Spain.

The perceived likelihood of Italy joining their ranks rose for the second consecutive week, up at 67 percent from a week ago. The probability of France, Germany, and Belgium launching the single currency on time was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.

European Union leaders reached an accord on a budget stability pact designed to ensure countries maintain fiscal discipline after they join the single currency. France also managed to get job creation back on the agenda, forcing through a resolution which gives the European Investment Bank a role in lending money for new employment programmes.
JP Morgan points out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
